      To each his own, but if you want to learn how to SPEAK a language, learning how to spell and write by hand is not always an efficient way to that goal. In fact, being too focused on the visual aspects of the language can cause pronunciation mistakes because many languages are not phonetically consistent in their spelling. Also, writing by hand is not the only way to commit things to memory at all. I prefer Anki's spaced repetition system with phrases and sentences that I've learned from friends, my teacher or from content in the target language. Also, Anki is something that you can do on the go because it's on your phone. Not everyone has so much time to sit and write out stuff regularly.

  Beginner:
  1. Find a good learning resource
  2. Get an understanding of  basic sentences
  3. Type notes and review them regularly
  4. Use the language!! Speak and write in it.
  
  Intermediate:
  1. High quality listening resource (ie. podcasts) designed for those learning the language
        -listen to the program every day while walking
       -repeat short phrases you understand, trying to match the speaker's pronunciation
       -when you're ready: repeat the word of phrase into Google translate
  
  Advanced:
  -talk with people in the target language
        -iTalki
        -HelloTalk
        -actually talk to someone irl

Also when you learn the words, learn them with their articles so you know if they are countale or uncountable.  For example, a book, some sugar.  Next, read The Clear Route to English Grammar.  It's lightyears ahead of everything else.  You can learn master most of English grammar in about two weeks.  Unless you just like wasting years on grammar, that's the way to go.

      @MANAHIL FATIMA ​ @MANAHIL FATIMA  you identify the role of a word in the sentence.
      in english and other western languages, you describe the role/position of a word in a sentence by saying: 
      this word is the subject, 
      this is the verb, 
      this is the object and it is accusative or dative.
      
      in arabic, it's the same; you just give a longer full detail description. for example, instead of saying: this word is the accusative object, you say: 
      
      "this is the verb in past tense for second-party plural speech. the standard clue to this grammatical classification is the .... sound at the end of the verb, but this sound was omitted in this case because the verb is augmented with a suffix whose pronunciation supersedes the original grammar law; the subject of the verb is omitted because it can be inferred from context, the first suffix is an augmented pronoun which plays the role of the first object, and the standard proof to this is the sound ..... at the end of the word, which has been omitted in this case because of the vowel at the end of the pronoun; the second suffix is an augmented pronoun which plays the role of the second object of the verb, and the standard clue to this is the sound ..... which has been ignored in this case because of impossibility to pronounce with the presence of the vowel at the end of the suffix"
      
      أعرب: سألتمونيها
      
      
      فعل ماض مبني على الفتحة المقدرة على آخره منع من ظهورها صيغة الجمع, و الفاعل ضمير مستتر تقديره أنتم, و "ني" ضمير متصل في محل نصب مفعول به أول منصوب بالفتحة المقدرة على آخره منع من ظهورها الضمير المتصل. "ها" ضمير متصل في محل نصب مفعول به ثان و علامة نصبه الفتحة المقدرة على آخره منع من ظهورها الالف
      
      
      the 5 lines i wrote above in english are the اعراب of one word + 3 suffixes augmented at the end of the word itself. this one word translates in english to a full sentence: "the questions which you have asked me". yes; that's one word in arabic with 3 suffixes.
      
      اعراب is pronounced "e'erab", and literally means: express, and in by convention when talking about grammar, it means: explain the role of the word
      
      if you understand what you're reading, it's easy. those with no brain will find it difficult because they memorize this stuff.
      how difficult is it to discern the object, subject, verb, and pronouns in a sentence!!!!
      but to be honest, the sentence i gave above is pretty standard. there are more sophisticated cases when a sentence contains:
      even i used to make mistakes sometimes
      an exception: they .... did them except him
      number: they did that twice
      reason: they did that in respect
      replacement: we, the people, did him
      redundant pronoun: they did them, all. they saw him, in person, in the flesh.
      joint objects: they did him and her
      calling: oh ....
      adjective: they did the tall guy
      adverbs: they did that slowly
      time / place: they did that at night on the floor
      complement / denounce: 
      exclamation:
      emphasis
      
      changing the order of subjects and objects, like Yoda speech:
      in the bed, there is a baby.

I loved them because of this teacher after Allah's blessing.
      Well why i loved it? after like eleven years hating Arabic ( as a grammar and الإعراب not the language itself ) how the heck did i love it? well that's because how it was taught to me from this teacher.   And mention, [O Muḥammad], in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east • And she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel [i.e., Gabriel], and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man • She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, [so leave me], if you should be fearing of Allāh." • He said, "I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you [news of] a pure boy [i.e., son]." • She said, "How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?" • He said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'" • So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place. • And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten." • But he called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream. • And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. • So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to [any] man.'" • Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented. • O sister [i.e., descendant] of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste." • So she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?" [Jesus] said, "Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. • And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakāh as long as I remain alive • And [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant  • And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive." • That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute. • It is not [befitting] for Allāh to take a son; exalted is He! When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.• [Jesus said], "And indeed, Allāh is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is a straight path.
   Surah maryam(mary)

      @تسنيم-ل4ذ  بص يا استاذه، فيه ناس ربنا كتب عليها الذله و المسكنه كده، مستعر من اصله و كاره كل اللي حوليه، فتلاقيه ييجي عند واحد كده لا بيه و لا عليه و يستفزه عشان التاني يهزقه فيحس هو انه عمل شيء...شيطان اعوذ بالله...اما عن موضوع الفلاحين، احب اقولك و خدها مني كلمه كاسكندراني متعصب كمان، الفلاحين ناس محترمه و ولاد اصول و علي راسنا، لكن الصق ليهم كلمه مشتقه ليس لها علاقه بيهم الا و هي 'الفلح' او ال'فلحنه'. و هي توجد في كتير من الناس و هي تساوي في المعني 'الشخص اللئيم او الخبيث' و تطور المعني بالعاميه مع الوقت ليشمل صفات ذميمه اخري، و اكرر هنا الالتباس، لان الكلمه ملهاش علاقه بالفلاح، لكن ببعض صفات المذمومين من الفلاحين، و الدنيا فيها ده و ده طبعا. 
      المشكل، ان بعض الفلاحين (ذوي النفوس الضعيفه) تلاقيهم يشتمو بلا سبب و لا داعي، غالبا علي النت للخوف من المواجهه، الناس في المدن كاسكندريه و القاهره بهذا اللفظ، و ديه موجه جديده موجهه من لجان معينه لتفريغ شحنه النقص و اشغال الناس في ما هو غير مهم، فينعتون اهل المدن بال'فلح'، و الطبيعي اهل المدن هيدافع ، مش عشان فاهم معني فلح او لانه بيكره الفلاحين، لكن لان كل واحد بيحب اصله و نفي الاصل عن شخص يعني نفيه شخصيا. فيحصل رد فعل و احيانا يتطور للسب لمن يعلمون معني 'فلح' و يشتعل الكلام و الناس اللي لا ليها في ده و لا ده تخسر بعض....شيطان! 
      لذلك اللي يقول علي اهل المدن فلح و ده شيء غير منطقي طبعا اعرف انه فلح مش فلاح و مستعر من اصله و يهوي الاستفزاز (معظمهم اخوانجيه و خلافه و بيكرهوا البلد و عاوزنها حريقه) عاشرت كتير منهم في الغربه! 
      بس للاسف لازم يتهزق و اخواننا الفلاحين بيفهموا ان الكلام عليهم هما
      
      اللي يقول لاهل المدن يافلاح فهموه بالادب انها مش شتيمه بس معلش كل واحد بيحب اصله و حكايه كلنا فلاحين دي اوفر شويه، مبنزرعش في المالح احنا، منطق يا اخواننا معلش
      
      و اللي يقول علي الفلاح فلح هزقوه و قولولو الفلاح راجل شريف و كفايه انهم علي الله و ناس طيبه 
      
      و اللي يقول بقي للفلاح يا فلاح قولولو و ماله و اسكتوا خلوه يتحرق من الصمت...هي مش شتيمه
      
      و اخيرا، كلنا مصريين، و كلمه لاخواننا من الريف، اجتنبوا مؤججي الفتن و متزيطوش لانهم بيكرهوا الناس فيكم

      @mrlegend7299  Wow good question- it has basically the exact meaning of "be my guest". But "suit yourself" is just slightly different...
      
      "Suit yourself" means "do what you like", but it is not welcoming like "be my guest" or "help yourself." 
      
      For example: "Want to walk to class with me?" "No, I'd rather walk alone." "Suit yourself."

      الكلمات الإنجليزية تنقرض كثيرًا في لهجاتنا, صحيح نتكلم بكلمات غريبة كثيرة, لكن أغلبها من أصل عربي.
      مثال: أنا فلسطيني, الكثير من الكلمات العبرية دخلت للهجتنا, لكن مع 3 أجيال تقريبًا استبدلنا معظمها بكلمات عربية, سواء فصحى أو عامية, فقط بعض العمال الصناعيين القدامى يستعملون أسماء عبرية لبعض الأدوات.
      الدارجة أكبر إختلاف في مخارج الحروف بها هو نطق حرف مد (الألف), بالنسبة لمعظمنا في الشرق, لفظكم له يشبه لفظة المد (ياء), و كذلك الفتحة لديكم تشبه لفظ الكسرة, و هذا يجعل فهم الكثير من الكلمات صعب.

      لكن عليك أن تعذر المصريين, حتى الدول المجاورة لها يجدون صعوبة في فهم لهجاتنا, لأن ثلث العرب مصريين و هذا يقلل من اختلاطهم بباقي العرب.

      @hamzabououden2305  سأجيبك بإختصار. كل المؤرخين دكروا أن الشعوب الأصلية لشمال إفريقيا هي (الجيتول السود الأفارقة , الحميريين ، الفينيقيين ) و عندما إستعمر الرومان شمال إفريقيا وجدوا فقط الحميريين و الفينيقيين و قامو بتسميتهم البربر. و بعد مدة جاء العرب الفاتحون لفتح شمال إفريقيا و تحريرها من الرومان. و ذالك ما حدت بالفعل. قام العرب بتحرير البربر من الرومان. البربر هم الفينيقيين و الحميريين. فبعد تحرير شمال إفريقيا من الرومان من طرف العرب قام العرب بإستيطان شمال إفريقيا مع إخوتهم البربر (الحميريين و الفينيقيين) مع العلم أن البربر كانت مساكنهم فقط هي الجبال و الكهوف كانو رحل بدو لا يعرفون التمدن كما دكرهم كل المؤرخون. و بعد إستيطان العرب لشمال إفريقيا قام العرب الأخرون بالهجرة إلى شمال إفريقيا أيضا و سمية هذه الهجرة بالتغريبة. ولم يدخل فقط بنو هلال وحدهم. بل دخلت مجموعة من القبائل العربية الكبيرة (بنو هلال و بنو سليم و بنو معقل و بنو حسان) و هذه ليست قبائل صغيرة. بل هي قبائل و أفخاد كبيرة من القبائل العربية الكبيرة. أما فحوصات الحمض النووي فقامت بإتبات أن شمال إفريقيا تحتوي على الجين العربي و الجين البربري الدي ترجع أصوله لليمن و الشام. و المدهل في الأمر أن هذا الجين البربري ليس بالجين القديم جدا . بل هو جين حديت ضهر فقط قبل الإسلام بقليل. أما قولك أن بنو هلال لا يمكن أن يكونو أغلبية في شمال إفريقيا فهذا مجرد كلام و ترترة. سكان أمريكا الأصليون هم الهنود الحمر و الأن أمريكا عبارة عن عرق أوروبي الأصل. ولا نسبة الهنود الحمر ضئيلة جدا و تكاد تكون شبه منعدمة. و هكذا ما صار مع البربر بحيت تمت إبادتهم من طرف الرومان و الوندال و أصبحوا مجرد أقلية. في الأخير العلم تطابق مع ما قاله كل المؤرخون العرب و الأجانب أن شمال إفريقيا تحتوي غالبية عربية من السعودية و الأقلية البربرية من اليمن و الشام و هذا ما قالته الفحوصات الجينية و الكتب التاريخية. أما مصطلح أمازيغ فلم يدكره أي مؤرخ. كل المؤرخين دكروا العرب و الفرس و المغول و البربر ولم يدكروا أن هناك شعب يسمى بالأمازيغ أبدا.

      ​ @BrianWilesOfficial What is (Islam ❤️)  ?
      
      Islam is the name of the religion, or more properly the ‘way of life’, which God (Allah) has revealed and which was practiced by all of the Prophets and Messengers of God that He sent to mankind.  Even the name stands out unique among other
      
      distorted religions in that it means a state of being; it does not refer to any particular person, such as Christianity, Buddhism or Zoroastrianism; a tribe like Judaism; or a nation like Hinduism.  The root Arabic word from which Islam is derived implies peace, safety, salutation, protection, blamelessness, wholesomeness, submission, acceptance, surrender, and salvation.  Islam specifically means being in the state of submission to God, worshipping Him Alone, and reverently accepting and obeying His Law.  Through this submission, the peace, security, and wholesome well-being implied in its literal meaning is achieved.  Hence, a Muslim or Muslimah is a person (male or female) in that state of submission.  A person’s Islam weakens through sins, ignorance, and wrong-doing, and becomes nullified in totality by associating partners with God or disbelieving in Him.

چيچل و سيدي بلعباس و المدية و بومرداس و أدرار و الشلف و الأغواط و أم البواقي و باتنة و بچاية و بسكرة و بشار و البليدة و البويرة و تمنراست و تيارت و تيزي وزو و الچلفة و سطيف و سعيدة و سكيكدة و عنابة و قالمة و قسنطينة و مستغانم و المسيلة و المعسكر و ورقلة و البيض و إليزي و الطارف و تندوف و تيسمسيلت و الوادي و خنشلة و سوق أهراس و تيبازة و ميلة و عين الدفلي و النعامة و عين تموشنت و غرداية و غليزان و نعرف تان أمثال چزايريه ما يعرفهاش غيركم نتوما الچزايريين: قلل ناسك يرتاح راسك و آتاي العشية خيرة من بقرة مشوية و اللي هاب الرچال هابوه و اللي باعك بالفول بيعو بالقشور و غيرهم بزاف بزاف . و انا تان نقدر نهدر مليح بزاف باللهچات: اللبنانية و السورية و الأردنية و الفلسطينية و الكويتية و العراقية و التونسية و المغربية و الليبية و باللغة الإنكليزية تان الحمدلله و ما علابالكش خو شحال انا نموت علي الچزاير و شحال نموت علي ناس الچزاير و شحال نموت علي اللهچة الچزايريه . اللهچة الچزايريه هدي شابة بزاف . نموت عليها بزاف و واحد الخطرة هدرت بيها مع واحد چزايري في الفايسبوك قال لي: راك چايب اللهچة صح و غاية تان و انا نترچم من هادو اللهچات: العراقية و التونسية و المغربية و الچزايريه و الليبية لأي لهچة عربية اخري . تحياتي من مصر ليك و لڨاع خاوتنا و أحبابنا بالچزاير ⁦☺️⁩🌹⁦🇪🇬⁩⁦🇩🇿⁩⁦♥️⁩⁦♥️⁩

  Deriving a new verb in turkish
  1.(Der-mek= ~to set layout & to provide)=ter'kib & ter'tib etmek (used after the verbs which ending with a consonant)
  Verb+"Der" is used as suffix for the subtle voiced words (ter-tir-tür/der-dir-dür/er-ir-ür)
  Verb+"Dar" is used as suffix for the thick voiced words  (tar-tır-tur/dar-dır-dur/ar-ır-ur)
  (ak-mak>aktarmak)(bakmak>baktırmak)(almak>aldırmak)(çıkmak>çıkarmak)(kaçmak>kaçırmak)
  
  2.(Et-mek = ~ to make) (mostly used after the verbs ending with a vowel sound and when the suffix "der" was used before)
  Verb+"T" is used as suffix for the subtle voiced words (t-it-üt)
  Verb+"T" is used as suffix for the thick voiced words (t-ıt-ut)
  (ak-mak>akıtmak)(bakmak>bakıtmak)(yürümek>yürütmek)(yırmak>yırtmak)(öldürmek>öldürtmek)
  
  3.(Eş=partner) (together or with partner)-(all together or altogether)-(each other or about each one)
  Verb+"Eş" is used as suffix for the subtle voiced words (eş-iş-üş)
  Verb+"Aş" is used as suffix for the thick voiced words (aş-ış-uş)
  (gör-mek-görüşmek) (bulmak>buluşmak)(uğramak-uğraşmak) (çalmak-çalışmak)
  
  4.(Al / El)= come to a state/a form through someone or something (to get being ...ed)
  Verb+"El" is used as suffix for the subtle voiced words (el-il-ül)
  Verb+"Al" is used as suffix for the thick voiced words (al-ıl-ul)
  (it's used as N to shorten some verbs)
  (gör-mek-görülmek) (satmak>-satılmak)(vermek>verilmek)(yemek>yeyilmek/yenmek)
  
  5."En"=own diameter(self environment)=(about own self)
  Verb+"En" is used as suffix for the subtle voiced words (en-in-ün)
  Verb+"An" is used as suffix for the thick voiced words (an-ın-un)
  (gör-mek>görünmek) (bulmak>bulunmak) (tıkamak>tıkanmak) (kıvırmak>kıvranmak)
  
  Mak/Mek...(emek)=exertion /process
  Git=Go (verb root) 
  Git-mek= to go (the process of going)>to get there
  (Git-der-mek>gittirmek)=1.Götürmek= to take away (2. Gidermek=~to resolve)
  (Git-en-der-mek>gidindirmek)= Göndermek= to send
  Gel-mek= to come
  (Gel-der-mek>geltirmek)=Getirmek= to bring
  1.Gelmek...2.Getirmek...3.Getirtmek...4.Getirttirmek..5.Getirttirtmek..and it's going so on
  
  Der-mek=  (~to provide) to set the layout by bringing together (der-le-mek= to compile)
  Dar-mak= to bring into a different order by disrupting the old (thara-mak=to comb)
  Dur-mak= to keep being present/there (~to remain/~to survive) (thor/hidher/hadeer/hızır)
  Dur-der-mak> durdurmak= ~to stop
  Dür-mek= to roll it up (to make it become a roll) 
  Dör-mek= to rotate on its axis ( törmek=old meaning)- to stir /to mix (current meaning)
  (döngü)törüş/törüv=tour (törüv-çi=turqui)(törüv-giş=turkish)=tourist...(thörük halk=mixed people in ownself)
  Törü-mek=türemek= to get created a new order by joining each other
  Töre=the order established over time= custom/tradition > (torah=sacred order) (tarih=history) 
  Törü-et-mek=türetmek= to create a new layout by adding them together= to derive

  (Dön-eş-mek)>dönüşmek= to turn (altogether) to something

  for positive sentences
  Var-mak= to arrive  (for the thick voiced words) (positive suffixes)=(Ar-ır-ur)
  Er-mek= to get (at)  (for the subtle voiced words) (positive suffixes)=(Er-ir-ür)
  
  for negative sentences 
  Ma=not

  (Kımıl Kımıl) kımıl-da-mak
  by colors
  Ak= white
  Ağar-mak = to turn to white
  Kara= black
  Karar-mak=to become blackened
  Kızıl= red
  Kızar-mak= to turn red (to blush) (to be toasted)
  by a whim or a want
  Su-sa-mak= to thirst
  Kanık-sa-mak
  öhö-tsu-ur (öksür-mek)=to cough
  tüh-tsu-ur (tüksür-mek/tükürmek)=to spit out 
  tıh-tsu-ur (tıksır-mak)
  hak-tsu-ur (aksır-mak)
  hap-tsu-ur (hapşur-mak)=to sneeze

  1. To knuckle down: to start focusing on your work / study.
  2. To get round to = to do smth you have intended to do, but you had not time. (Useful for 'Can you' questions).
  3. To while away = to spend time in a relaxed   way (useful for talking about hobbies).
  4. To brush up on = to improve a skill you havent practiced for some time.
  ‐---------------
  5. To bank on = to expect and hope smth will happen (useful for answering future questions in part 3).
  6. To be in for = to be about to have or experience smth = experience sth in the future.
  7. To pan out = to result or develop in a certain way.
  8. To run up against = to face problems or difficult situations.
  -----------------
  9. To mull over = to think carefully about smth (useful for 'what do you think of...' questions).
  10. To figure out = to find solution.
  -----------------
  'Do you agree that the government should...?'
  11. To get on with = to start or continue doing smth.
  12. To buckle down = to start working hard.
  -----------------
  Describe a thing / a person
  13. To stumble upon = to find it by chance.
  14. To bump into = to meet someone by chance / accident.
  15. To turn out = to happen in a certain way.

      Native English here, our language is technically the same, but subtly different in a lot of ways :)
       I think American English is much more accessible and honestly nicer sounding. English (native) drops a lot of prepositions and takes on glottal stops. We've basically butchered our language to the point that northern spoken English is its own creature :) If you want to see the car-crash that is native English just look at our place names, they have retained the original pronunciations from the Vikings,Danes,Celts,Gaelic,Welsh and Saxon.

    ↳ **@yhwang2884** (👍71 · 2021-08-12) — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bwsrXgaYNkE&lc=UgwY2u3kQImGQ5DhsNx4AaABAg.9LOYfkJcQAI9LfwG55zBnu
      1. To knuckle down: to start focusing on your work/study.
      eg. I word as a teacher and we've got an exam coming soon so we all need to knuckle down. 
      
      
      2. To get round to = to do smth you have intended to do, but you had not time. (Useful for 'Can you' questions).
      eg. I would love to learn how to cook, but I just haven't got round to it. I've been too busy. 
      
      
      3. To while away = to spend time in a relaxed way (useful for talking about hobbies).
      eg. I love to while away the afternoon watching movies. 
      
      
      4. To brush up on = to improve a skill you haven't practiced for some time.
      
      eg. I love playing the guitar, but I need to brush up on it because I haven't played for some time. 
      
      5. To bank on = to expect and hope smth will happen (useful for answering future questions in part 3).
      eg. I am banking on the covid situation getting better next year.  
      Many governments are banking on the economy improving in the future.
      
      6. To be in for = to be about to have or experience smth.
      eg. We are in for a few surprises in the future.
      Many real shops are in for a hard time next year, as most people will choose to shop online.
      
      
      7. To pan out = to result or develop in a certain way.
      eg. I think things will get better, but we will have to see how things pan out. 
      I think our goal of getting everyone vaccinated this year, isn't going to pan out. 
      
      8. To run up against = to face problems or difficult situations.
      
      eg. I think we are going to run up against a lot of problems in this area. 
      We are going to run up against more crime in the future. 
      
      
      9. To mull over = to think carefully about smth (useful for 'what do you think of...' questions).
      eg. I've been mulling (this) over this a lot recently and I think...
      
      
      10. To figure out = to find a solution.
      
      eg. It's complicated and it's not easy to figure out a solution. 
      
      
      'Do you agree that the government should...?'
      11. To get on with = to start or continue doing smth.
      eg. The government talks about reducing the crime rate, but they just need to get on with it.
      
      12. To buckle down = to start working hard.
      eg. It's time the government buckled down and found a solution. 
      
      
      Describe a thing / a person
      13. To stumble upon = to find it by chance. (things)
      eg. I'd like to tell you about a great book that I stumbled on recently.
      
      
      14. To bump into = to meet someone by chance/accident.
      eg. Recently I bumped into an old friend and he.....
      
      
      15. To turn out = to happen in a certain way.
      eg. It was a difficult time but in the end everything turned out fine(well).
      
      I added all the example sentences in the video and try to help you to understand how to use them. And thank other comtributors.

  Shouldn't it be 'wrongly'? I realise that 'wrong' is commonly used now, but I still regard 'wrongly' as the correct adverb to use in this sense. To exemplify further, a synonym of 'wrongly' is 'incorrectly' - and we would never think of saying 'Are you saying it incorrect?' I hope not, anyway. The more these 'mistakes' are used, the more commonly accepted they become. But it still jars when I hear intelligent people like Sir Geoffrey Hinton, the 'godfather of AI', saying 'AI will soon be smarter than us.' No, Sir Geoffrey! 'AI will soon be smarter than we are (smart).' It's a mistake that AI would never make! Likewise, too, the replacement of 'less' for 'fewer' when the distinction is easy to make: 'fewer' for countable items that can be enumerated (fewer apples), 'less' for uncountable items (less water). I know this all sounds horribly pedantic. But it's the kind of thing that leads to laziness and confusion. After all, if we made these kinds of mistakes doing something like coding, we'd end up with buggy programs!
